chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Size of the band and meeting Ivie Anderson
summary: The band was fourteen plus Ivie, dancers Snake Hips Tucker and Bessie Dudley; Ivie was the only member he knew in California.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Were there additional members of the band by that time? I read in one place Barry White they were giving out quotes some news report saying 13 members of the were coming and I know that must be wrong.
And then later he makes reference to 18. How many -- was the band enlarged when it got to England?
No, we carried a couple of dancers and people like that. We could have had 18. Till very late we had 16 and then the singer --
They had a singer so it all could have made up --
Was that -- it was a 14 piece band plus Ivy.
14 piece band and Ivy Anderson. Then they carried Snake Hips Tucker and Bessie Dudley and a couple of people like that. Then later on they carried three or four -- we had three singers.
You had known Ivy at the Apex in Los Angeles. Had you known anybody else who was in the band before you joined, or was Ivy the only person you had ever met before?

Ivy was the only one I'd met in California except the members when they came to California. They played California in '30 when they came out to make the Amos and Andy picture.

I didn't join till '32 which was the second time they came out.
Oh, practically all of them. Johnny, Sonny, especially Sonny. And practically all of the band.
I read that Ivy had worked in a place called Tate's in Los Angeles before she joined Duke. Where was Tate's -- do you know?
That's before my time too. I don't remember.
